page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, placing the instance in the top 25% of tested servers in stress-ng and PassMark CPU evaluations. The AMD EPYC architecture supports AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, which contribute to strong performance in cryptographic operations and extended instruction tests. Memory performance is mixed; cached read-only small-block memory bandwidth is in the top 25%, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the middle 50%.

The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations, all scoring in the top 25%. For language model workloads, it processes prompts and generates text efficiently on small 135M models, though performance drops to average levels for medium 7B models. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration represents a clear tradeoff, making this instance less suitable for heavy deep learning training or high-I/O local storage tasks, but highly efficient for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and parallel processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates strong performance in multi-core CPU execution, cryptography, and database operations, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. However, uncached memory bandwidth and text processing fall into the average range. With a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, this instance is designed for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and small-scale language model inference, offering a balanced resource density for parallel processing tasks without local storage dependencies.
